title: Equivalence operations on relative universal cones
statement:
Use quasicategories, functor equivalences, coherent transformations and right-pinched mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the relative universal diagrams of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], using its path-pullback model for strictly commuting squares of Kan complexes. The quasicategory and Kan-mapping-space assertions needed for these squares are supplied by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Inner fibrations have the meaning of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]; an isofibration between quasicategories is an inner fibration lifting equivalence edges with any specified source over the source of the given edge. All objects are small in a fixed sufficiently large universe. The following equivalence operations preserve relative universal diagrams.
(1) Let $M$ be any small simplicial set. If $p:D\to B$ is a functor of quasicategories and $q,q':M^{\triangleright}\to D$ are naturally equivalent as coherent diagrams, then $q$ is a $p$-colimit diagram if and only if $q'$ is.
(2) Let $p:D\to B$ be an inner fibration of quasicategories, $e:L\to M$ an equivalence of quasicategories, $f:M\to D$ and $g:M^{\triangleright}\to B$ satisfy $pf=g|_M$. The existence of a $p$-colimit diagram $q:M^{\triangleright}\to D$ with $q|_M=f$ and $pq=g$ is equivalent to the existence of one on $L^{\triangleright}$ with boundary $fe$ and base $ge^{\triangleright}$. For any particular $q:M^{\triangleright}\to D$, it is a $p$-colimit diagram if and only if $qe^{\triangleright}$ is one.
(3) If $p:D\to B$ is an inner fibration of quasicategories, $M$ a quasicategory with final object $t$, and $q:M^{\triangleright}\to D$ a $p$-colimit diagram, then its edge $a:q(t)\to q(*)$ is $p$-cocartesian. Here $p$-cocartesian has the horn-lifting meaning of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. If $p(a)$ is an equivalence, then $a$ is an equivalence.
(4) Define the opposite simplicial set by precomposition with order reversal on the simplex category: an operator $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ is replaced by $j\mapsto n-\alpha(m-j)$. Opposites of quasicategories are quasicategories; opposites of isofibrations are isofibrations. For every quasicategory $D$ and vertices $x,y$, there are natural equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_{D^{\mathrm{op}}}(x,y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_D(y,x)$. For a small simplicial set $M$ and a functor $p:D\to B$ of quasicategories, under $(M^{\triangleleft})^{\mathrm{op}}\cong(M^{\mathrm{op}})^{\triangleright}$, a diagram $q:M^{\triangleleft}\to D$ is a $p$-limit diagram if and only if $q^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a $p^{\mathrm{op}}$-colimit diagram. For any quasicategory $C$ and vertex $c$, the opposite of $C_{c/}$ is canonically $(C^{\mathrm{op}})_{/c}$, respecting the entire remaining face and the canonical cone/cocone. The corresponding duals of (1)-(3) hold.
